BiblicalUsage: I take gᵉbûwlâh to mean border, boundary, nothing more and nothing less. It occurs 10 times, and Numbers and Deuteronomy show it doing ordinary work in ordinary sentences. The Bible uses plain words plainly, and this is one of them.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that gᵉbûwlâh matters because God sets boundaries, and His boundaries are for our good. My position is that Scripture does not hide its meaning from honest readers.
